entities.name: UBE2I / UBC9
observations: UBC9 knockdown in cardiomyocytes reduced GFPu/CL1 reporter-based UPS activity and increased aggregated protein in a CryAB(R120G) proteotoxicity model.
UBC9 overexpression enhanced UPS activity, reduced CryAB(R120G)-associated aggregates, and increased autophagic flux in cardiac proteotoxicity models.
Cardiomyocyte-specific Ubc9 knockout aggravated diabetic cardiomyopathy and impaired mitophagy; the reported mechanism involved NEDD4/RUNX2/PSEN2 and was described as SUMOylation-independent.

entities.name: Cardiac proteotoxicity
observations: CryAB(R120G)-associated cardiomyocyte proteotoxicity is worsened by UBC9 loss and ameliorated by UBC9 overexpression, with effects on UPS activity and protein aggregate burden.

entities.name: Cardiomyocyte proteostasis
observations: UBC9 supports cardiomyocyte protein quality control through UPS function, aggregate handling, autophagic flux, and mitophagy, especially under proteotoxic or metabolic stress.

entities.name: PMID:25097219
observations: UBC9 is required for efficient protein quality control in cardiomyocytes; knockdown impaired UPS activity and increased protein aggregation, while overexpression was protective in CryAB(R120G) proteotoxicity.

entities.name: PMID:27142163
observations: UBC9-mediated SUMOylation increased autophagic activity and improved cardiac proteotoxic disease phenotypes in CryAB(R120G) models.

observations: Cardiomyocyte-specific Ubc9 knockout worsened diabetic cardiomyopathy and impaired mitophagy; evidence accessed from the abstract.
